decision_reason: The public IRD Forge project page describes RQC as an NGS-read quality-control workflow, and its tree contains functional workflow code and a direct AGPL-3.0 root license. However, the repository README is actually the GeVarLi manual, not RQC documentation; I found no separate RQC install/use guide, versioned distribution, or exact-product operational adoption. The project identity and notability path therefore need correction or independent evidence before admission.

government_provenance.note: The exact project is hosted in the IRD Forge TransVIHMI namespace and its landing-page description names RQC, but the repository's mismatched README does not establish the sponsoring agency or relationship beyond the namespace.

public_source.note: The project is publicly accessible without credentials and exposes RQC workflow/source files, including workflow/snakefiles/quality_control.smk.

eligible_license.note: The repository root contains the full GNU Affero General Public License version 3 text. This establishes an eligible grant for the observed project-authored code; it does not resolve product identity or agency sponsorship.

primary_evidence.note: The project landing-page description says RQC performs raw NGS read quality control, but the README names GeVarLi and documents SARS-CoV-2 genome analysis instead. No RQC-specific usage/deployment page or versioned release was found; reconcile the documentation or provide exact-product use evidence.

product_identity: Reads Quality Control (RQC), described as a raw NGS-read quality-control workflow; identity/docs conflict with GeVarLi README
agency: Unresolved; IRD/TransVIHMI namespace is visible but project-specific sponsor attribution not established
license: AGPL-3.0 root grant for observed source; product-level admission on hold
family_note: Do not merge with GeVarLi based on the README copied/served in this repository; establish whether this is an independent RQC workflow or a repository/documentation mistake.
status_note: GitLab project API reports creation on 2022-03-15, but this is not used as a first licensed-source year because the exact product, sponsoring agency, and product-specific documentation remain unresolved. The live README currently describes GeVarLi, while the project landing page describes RQC.

decision_reason: SLAM is an IRD-authored, reusable utility that generates and optionally submits SLURM job scripts for the i-Trop HPC cluster. The 2024 license-bearing source snapshot already contains the functional v.2024.02 Bash tool and user guide; the current repository documents the 2026.05 Python rewrite. Its direct AGPL-3.0 grant, explicit versioned source, and user instructions satisfy the four checks and the agency-published operational-tool pathway.

government_provenance.note: The exact product README identifies Nicolas Fernandez and other contributors as IRD staff and says the utility targets the i-Trop cluster. IRD's official i-Trop page confirms the cluster is an operational HPC service using SLURM: https://bioinfo.ird.fr/index.php/en/cluster-2/.

public_source.note: The canonical IRD Forge project is public without credentials and exposes the Bash and Python implementations, README, and license.

eligible_license.note: The exact 2024-02-16 snapshot contains the full AGPL-3.0 text. The same commit tree contains SLAM.sh and its v.2024.02 README, so this is a grant-bearing functional source snapshot rather than a later metadata-only license addition.

primary_evidence.note: The exact-product guide explains invocation/options and direct sbatch submission, identifies the i-Trop cluster, and documents version 2026.05. The official cluster page confirms i-Trop is an operational SLURM HPC service with user account and software-installation processes: https://bioinfo.ird.fr/index.php/en/cluster-2/.

product_identity: SLAM (SLURM Lightweight Automated Manager), an IRD utility to generate and optionally submit job scripts for the i-Trop HPC cluster
agency: Institut de recherche pour le développement (IRD), i-Trop HPC/Bioinformatics platform
family_note: Standalone operational helper for SLURM users, not the i-Trop scheduler or the SLAM acronym's unrelated products.
status_note: The first directly inspected grant-bearing snapshot is commit 6c13a1a (2024-02-16); it contains the v.2024.02 Bash SLAM.sh and README. The project was later refactored to Python; its current VERSION and README identify 2026.05, with last source activity 2026-05-20. No Git tags were present, but versioned source snapshots and user guidance are documented. Official cluster details: https://bioinfo.ird.fr/index.php/en/cluster-2/.

decision_reason: CRDAP is an exact IRD/UAR191 oceanographic data-acquisition and processing environment, with official reports documenting real campaign use and public installation guidance. The root GPL-3.0-only grant is direct, but the product repository delegates material acquisition/processing functions to six separately linked submodule repositories; their grants and product-wide license scope have not been reconciled. Hold the product-level license and source-year conclusions until those components are audited.

government_provenance.note: The official IRD UAR191/IMAGO 2021 activity report names CRDAP and records its evolution. The repository is in the US191/IRD namespace; a 2019 official report also documents CRDAP use to acquire/process data during a named oceanographic campaign: https://imago.ird.fr/content/download/325802/4978105/version/1/file/2019_RAPPORT_ACTIVITE_BREST.pdf.

public_source.note: The canonical repository is public without credentials and contains source, configuration, documentation, and a root LICENSE.

eligible_license.note: The main repository grants GPL-3.0-only for its own contents, but .gitmodules links six separate functional repositories (ctdSeaProcessing, LADCP, plots, oceano2python, oceano2kml, chemicalprocessing). Do not extend the root grant to those components without checking each grant and their inclusion/distribution scope: https://forge.ird.fr/us191/crdap/-/blob/master/.gitmodules. The installation guide also documents a MATLAB-licensed processing path.

primary_evidence.note: The official UAR191 report describes CRDAP and its Docker image being used to set up/validate acquisition and processing tools during the MARACAS7 campaign. Later official 2021 reporting records CRDAP evolution, while the project wiki provides installation instructions: https://forge.ird.fr/us191/crdap/-/wikis/Installation.

product_identity: CRDAP (Cruise Repository for Data Acquisition and Processing), an umbrella environment for oceanographic cruise acquisition and processing
agency: Institut de recherche pour le développement (IRD), UAR191/IMAGO
geography: France; oceanographic campaigns including international waters
license: GPL-3.0-only for main-repository contents; whole-product/submodule licensing unresolved
family_note: Multi-repository application/data-processing environment. Six `.gitmodules` components are distinct codebases and the root GPL grant is not presumed to relicense them.
status_note: Official 2019 and 2021 activity reports establish exact-product campaign use and subsequent evolution. GitLab activity continues into July 2026. The installation wiki requires several third-party systems and documents MATLAB licensing for some processing; resolve the six submodule grants and clarify the product boundary before assigning a first public licensed-source year or catalog-wide license.

In addition, the repository has no versioned release, documented independent reuse, or verified production/research deployment; its public CMake build instructions alone do not meet the notability baseline. The source was last active in 2022.
